sentences.text: Kamal Narayan Verma S/o Shri Rewa Ram, Aged About 29 Years, R/o -  Village - Nardaha, P.S. - Mandir Hasoud, District (Civil and Revenue) - Raipur  (C.G.), Chhattisgarh  ---- Applican  Versus   State Of Chhattisgarh Through District Magistrate, Raipur, District Raipur  (C.G.), Chhattisgarh  ---- Non-applicant
For Applicant - Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Advocate.

For State - Mr. Sudhir Sahu, Panel Lawyer.
 Hon'ble Shri Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey  Order on Board 12-10-2022 1.

By this revision the applicant has challenged the legality and propriety of the judgment dated 06-01-2014 passed by the III rd Additional Sessions Judge, Raipur in Criminal Appeal No.201/2012 affirming the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 03-11-2012 passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur in Criminal Case No.655/2007 whereby the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur has convicted the applicant under Section 16(1)(a)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for six months and to pay fine of Rs.1000/-, in default of payment of fine further R.I. for one month.

entities.text: III rd Additional Sessions Judge, Raipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Mr. Yogesh Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the case of N. Sukumaran Nair vs Food Inspector, Mavelikara, (1997) 9 SCC 101 in the similar situation Hon'ble Supreme Court has directed the State Government for taking appropriate steps for commutation of the sentence on deposit of Rs.6,000/- in terms of Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Cr.P.C.

entities.text: N. Sukumaran Nair vs Food Inspector, Mavelikara, (1997) 9 SCC 101
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submitted that in the present case the applicant who was not a manufacturer of red lentils ( elwj nky) and he was only selling it in his grocery shop and the same was found adulterated.

He further submits that the complaint case was filed on 26-08-2003 and he was convicted by the learned trial Kamal Narayan Verma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7341284/

sentences.text: Court on 03-11-2012, and appeal preferred by him was dismissed on 06-01-2014 and thus, he is facing trial since 2003.
3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State submits that the applicant was running a grocery shop from where red lentils ( elwj nky) and tea leaves were purchased by the Food Inspector.
The samples taken from the grocery shop were sent for analysis, red lentils (elwj nky) was found adulterated.
He further submits that the prosecution has proved guilt of the present applicant beyond reasonable doubt and there is concurrent finding recorded by both the Courts below.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

5. Hon'ble Supreme Court while dealing with similar issue in the case of N. Sukumaran Nair vs Food Inspector, Mavelikara (supra) has observed in para 3 as under:-
"3..

entities.text: N. Sukumaran Nair vs Food Inspector, Mavelikara
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The offence took place in the year 1984.
The appellant has been awarded six months' simple imprisonment and has also been ordered to pay a fine of Rs. 1000/-.
Under Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, "the appropriate government" is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.
We think that this would be an appropriate case for commutation of sentence where almost a decade has gone by.

We, therefore, direct the appellant to deposit in the trial court a sum of Rs, 6000/- as fine in commutation of the sentence of six months' simple imprisonment within a period of six weeks from today and intimate to the appropriate government that such fine has been deposited.
On deposit of such fine, the Stale Government may formalise the matter by passing appropriate orders under Clause (d) of Section 433 of the CrPC. "

6. Considering the fact that the complaint case was filed in the year 2003, the applicant is not a manufacturer of the red lentils ( elwj nky), he is facing trial since 2003, therefore, ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of N. Sukumaran Nair vs Food Inspector, Mavelikara (supra) can be applied in the present case.

entities.text: N. Sukumaran Nair vs Food Inspector, Mavelikara
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Consequently, this revision is partly allowed.

Conviction of the applicant under Section 16(1)(a)(1)
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is hereby maintained.

He is directed to deposit fine of Rs.6000/- before learned trial Court and he is permitted to move application before the appropriate Government for commutation of the imprisonment within two months from receipt of copy of this order.
It is made clear that if the sentence is not commuted by the appropriate Government, then the applicant shall make himself available before the learned trial Court for serving remaining sentence.
8. With the aforesaid observation, this criminal revision is disposed off.
